analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/provider/sandboxes.md (head lines 21-23, 30-43, 65-71, 155-166, 214) and docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md (new 'The cluster waitlist' section at head lines 49-73). No source, protocol, key-handling or authorization code is touched, so I found no regression in the trust boundaries or controls of TB-002, TB-011, TB-012, TB-013 or TB-014, nor in T-041 or the other listed threats.

What the docs now describe: an account-level waitlist (`darkbloom waitlist sandbox|cluster`) that sends nothing about the Mac, gates `darkbloom sandbox setup` and new-pair `darkbloom cluster`, and exempts already-paired Macs. The docs also state that setup never passes the installer's `--force`. These are described as product behavior, and no changed code in this batch implements them.

T-061 (installer download run as the owner) is unchanged. The docs still say the installer verifies the release and that nothing is installed before the user answers `y`. The docs do not weaken the TB-013 consent step.

Unverified contract: whether the CLI actually enforces the waitlist check, does not leak Mac identifiers to the waitlist request, and honors the paired-Mac exemption is implemented in code outside this batch, so I cannot confirm it. The docs claim 'sending nothing about this Mac'; a code-side pass should verify that against the waitlist request implementation. The cluster-doc exemption for already-paired Macs is a product policy, not a security control, and is not a trust boundary from the supplied evidence.

The two-mac-cluster.md base text was only partly supplied (about line 448), but the patch is complete and adds one self-contained section with no overlap with security-relevant statements.

No threat-model updates are required from these doc changes alone.
